criteria: COMMON_SPEC §2.C relations, evaluated separately per partition and build over situations extracted by gamewatch/gw2/situations.ts; law clauses checked outcome field by outcome field (full support only when every expected outcome is recorded and matches; partial support kept separate); invariance clauses by disjoint recorded value sets across different combinations of the varied fields, with comparison partners; unknown fields excluded as missing evidence; the combined reading is matched per situation and outcome field; denominators count unique situations, clause checks, outcome checks and case/match units separately
caveat: Every verdict is scoped to the evaluated situations. Finite observations do not establish a rule for situations that were not evaluated, and fitting observations does not identify a unique rule.

inventory.reason: Board geometry, start squares and scoring are not represented by the P4 situation kinds (no movement or scoring situation).
Turn alternation, game end and tie-breaks need game-level situations that P4 does not extract.

inventory.scope: Turn starts only: the number of move actions granted at the start of a turn (actionsGranted) from the own pieces on the board and the extra actions earned for that turn.

inventory.reason: Stacking and capture need movement situations that P4 does not extract.
Placement legality needs placement situations (refused/accepted placements) that P4 does not extract.
The referee procedure is not an observable outcome of a single situation.

inventory.scope: Effect entries recorded with board states (scripted cases): entries that agree on effect kind, arrival, whether the piece was shielded and whether the chain cap applied must have the same observable outcome (fired, absorbed, cell used up, shield afterwards) whichever side owns the piece and whichever side owns the effect.

Effect entries that are not past the chain cap: the entered cell is used up afterwards, by own move or forced arrival; an unshielded piece sets the effect off; the other cells of a multi-cell effect stay.

inventory.reason: The chain cap itself is not checked (it would need the chain length per arrival); R8 uses the recorded chain-limit event as an input.
Shove distances and directions need movement outcomes that P4 does not extract.
Freeze duration needs move-refusal situations that P4 does not extract.
Send-home destinations need movement outcomes that P4 does not extract.
Teleport destinations are random; no P4 situation represents them.

inventory.scope: Effect entries by a piece that was shielded before entering (scripted cases), not past the chain cap: the effect does not apply (absorbed, not fired), the shield is used up, and the cell is used up.

inventory.reason: Who receives the extra action is not an extracted outcome; R3 uses recorded extra-action events as inputs.
